candidates.name: ETH continuous-state drift filter
candidates.economicMechanism: Persistent directional demand may support a sufficiently large, slow ETH drift after costs.
candidates.information: ETH completed closes; causal EWMA of past squared log returns.
equations: Before observation t: R=max(1e-8, prior EWMA squared return); Q=diag(.01R,.0001R).
Enter if 14*drift - 14*sqrt(P_drift,drift)>base log round-trip cost; exit if drift<=0; otherwise retain target.
candidates.initialization: First log close, zero drift, P=diag(.0016,.0016/90), EWMA=.0016; filter from bar 1, suppress targets before index 90.
candidates.nearestPriorFamily: ETH40 trend and the previous HMM/BOCPD inference prototypes.
candidates.materialDifference: A continuous two-state posterior and covariance-dependent entry hurdle; no discrete latent-state bank or fixed lookback close mean.
candidates.novelty: Established inference template applied to ETH; no original mathematics or distinct economic source claimed.
candidates.nullAndFailure: Filtered drift need not persist. Gaussian assumptions, changes in volatility, and slow reversals can produce losses; the state-uncertainty penalty excludes future process risk.

candidates.name: ETH mature-label BTC context regression
candidates.economicMechanism: A lagged BTC/ETH return relationship could predict ETH continuation or catch-up over 14 days.
candidates.information: ETH and BTC closes through t; only historical 14-day outcomes fully realized by t enter training.
equations: At t>=28, mature label y=log(ETH_t/ETH_(t-14)) for regressor x_(t-14).
After at least 60 matured labels and index 90, enter if mu-meanPenalty>base log round-trip cost; exit if mu<=0; otherwise retain.
candidates.initialization: beta=0, inverse information=identity, residual variance=.01; first feature at 14, first mature update at 28.
candidates.nearestPriorFamily: Relative-strength rotation and fixed-window momentum; generic regression prototypes elsewhere are not new mathematics.
candidates.materialDifference: Causal fitted conditional ETH forecast with BTC context and explicit label maturation. It never rotates into BTC. Learning parameters respond to realized forecast errors.
candidates.novelty: Established recursive least squares; new candidate application, not an original estimator or independent alpha source.
candidates.nullAndFailure: Cross-asset predictability may be absent or unstable; overlapping outcomes violate independent-error interpretations, so the mean penalty is not a calibrated confidence bound.

candidates.name: ETH close-location volume pressure
candidates.economicMechanism: High-volume closes near the daily high may indicate persistent directional participation.
candidates.information: ETH daily high, low, close and native venue volume.
equations: Enter when pressure>.15 and C_t>C_(t-1); exit when pressure<-.05; otherwise retain.
candidates.initialization: Cash; no entry before index 90. A zero volume window has pressure zero.
candidates.nearestPriorFamily: Indicator hysteresis, with volume and intrabar close location replacing the price-only statistic.
candidates.materialDifference: Identical close histories can give different targets when high/low/volume histories differ.
candidates.novelty: Chaikin-style established indicator. Under the prior strict structural protocol this is a feature variant, not a certified new mathematical system family.
candidates.nullAndFailure: A close-location statistic is not actual signed order flow; a gap down may coexist with positive pressure. Native venue volume may not represent global ETH demand.

candidates.name: ETH drawdown recovery state machine
candidates.economicMechanism: A large selloff followed by recovery could reflect temporary liquidity pressure followed by replenished demand.
candidates.information: ETH closes, trailing 90-close peak, and remembered peak/trough for an armed event.
equations: In IDLE at t>=90, arm if C_t<=.80*max(C_(t-89)..C_t); save that peak and trough=C_t.
In ARMED, trough=min(trough,C_t). Enter if C_t>=1.08*trough and C_t<savedPeak.
In LONG, exit if C_t>=savedPeak or C_t<=savedTrough or t-entryIndex>=42.
After exit suppress arming through exitIndex+6; return to IDLE on exitIndex+7.
candidates.initialization: IDLE, cash, with no prewarmup event state. One transition branch per completed bar.
candidates.nearestPriorFamily: Trend-conditioned reversion and channel breakout; common drawdown recovery and trailing-stop ideas.
candidates.materialDifference: Event-specific peak/trough remain after their original observations leave a fixed lookback. Entry requires an ordered drawdown then recovery sequence.
candidates.novelty: A fixed heuristic state policy within the known recovery/reversion parent. New implementation and trial; independent structural novelty unresolved.
candidates.nullAndFailure: A rebound may be a pause in a longer decline. Remembered barriers are close-signal conditions followed by delayed execution, not guaranteed stop prices.
